title: Why String is Immutable
question: Why is String immutable in Java? What are the benefits?
searchIntent: why is string immutable in java interview
realWorldScenario: String immutability enables the String pool, safe HashMap keys, and thread-safe sharing of string constants.

title: String Pool
question: What is the String pool (String constant pool) in Java? How does it work?
searchIntent: what is string constant pool java
realWorldScenario: When you write String s = "hello" twice, both reference the same object in the pool, saving memory.

title: String new vs Literal
question: What is the difference between String s = "hello" and String s = new String("hello")?
searchIntent: string literal vs new String java
realWorldScenario: A classic interview == trap: two string literals are equal (==), but new String() creates a heap object that fails ==.

title: StringBuilder vs StringBuffer
question: What is the difference between StringBuilder and StringBuffer? When do you use each?
searchIntent: StringBuilder vs StringBuffer when to use
realWorldScenario: Single-threaded string building uses StringBuilder (faster); multi-threaded use StringBuffer (synchronized).

title: String concat vs StringBuilder
question: Why is String concatenation with + in a loop inefficient? What should you use instead?
searchIntent: why is string concatenation in loop bad java
realWorldScenario: Concatenating 10,000 strings in a loop with + creates 10,000 intermediate String objects, causing GC pressure.

title: String.intern()
question: What does String.intern() do in Java?
searchIntent: what does string intern do java
realWorldScenario: intern() forces a heap string into the pool, allowing == comparison — rarely needed in modern Java.
